topPRs.title: kona: Add in-process zkVM canary for kona-sp1
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Overview

Adds `kona-zkvm-canary`, a long-running service that continuously executes the published Kona `super-range` guest against finalized live-network inputs using SP1’s CPU executor.

The canary executes both range and consolidation modes, compares their outputs with the native results produced during witness collection, and reports correctness failures without generating proofs or submitting work to the Succinct Prover Network.

This service is analogous to the vm-runner (op-challenger runner).

## What changed

- Added a finalized snapshot source that:
  - selects consecutive finalized timestamps;
  - pins L1 at `min(CurrentL1 - 1, L1 finalized)`;
  - validates super-root proofs, chain coverage, safety horizons, and span linkage;
  - resolves reported L1 identities against the configured L1 RPC;
  - classifies malformed or inconsistent parent data as `input_error`.
- Added in-process, sequential SP1 execution for range and consolidation modes.
- Added explicit SP1 cycle and memory limits.
  - Cycle-limit exhaustion is reported as `cycle_limit_exceeded`, never as a guest rejection.
  - The wall-clock deadline covers cancellable selection and witness stages only.
- Added fingerprint-based scheduling:
  - successful fingerprints are not rerun;
  - correctness failures receive one confirmation attempt;
  - attempts never overlap and cadence starts after completion.
- Added graceful shutdown during cancellable stages. A signal during uncancellable SP1 execution
  terminates the process and leaves restart handling to the orchestrator.
- Added startup artifact authentication:
  - loads `<prestate>.range.bin.gz`;
  - bounds compressed and decompressed sizes;
  - verifies the decompressed ELF SHA-256 and SP1 verification key;
  - keeps the authenticated ELF entirely in memory.
- Added structured, credential-redacted logging.
- Added Prometheus metrics for lifecycle, outcomes, target progress, stage durations, aggregate SP1 reports, artifact identity, and process memory.
  - Per-phase cycle and invocation totals remain in structured report logs rather than Prometheus series.
- Added `--once` for manual diagnostics using the normal execution path and existing `EXIT_VALID`, `EXIT_INVALID`, and `EXIT_INFRA` conventions.
- Added Melange/APKO packaging and image routing for a non-root, binary-only `kona-zkvm-canary` image. The guest ELF is not embedded in the image.
- Documented configuration, trust boundaries, execution bounds, metrics, and one-shot operation.

## Operational decisions

- Execution is in-process because SP1 already moves emulator work onto Tokio’s blocking pool.
- SP1 execution is not wrapped in a Tokio timeout because `spawn_blocking` work cannot be
  cancelled. The SP1 cycle limit is the resource-reclaiming execution bound.
- Finalized supernode responses are assumed immutable for a timestamp. The selected snapshot stays
  in memory for the attempt and is not fetched again after execution.
- The service writes no files. The sp1-sdk `TRACE_FILE` is rejected during configuration.
- Configuration and artifact authentication complete before the metrics listener is bound.
- `/health` comes from `kona-sp1-host-utils`; no readiness gauge or dedicated readiness behavior
  was added.
- No canary guest execution was added to CI, acceptance tests, or devstack.

Part of #18325

topPRs.title: kona-sp1: add multi-cycle proposer policy scenarios
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds comprehensive multi-cycle proposer policy coverage using the deterministic `ScenarioWorld` and `ScenarioHarness`.

The scenarios cover:

- Frozen proposal horizons and long foreign-game histories
- Concurrent defense while creation is stalled
- Trusted and untrusted superroot contradictions
- Timed-out creation, late inclusion, and duplicate-creation guards
- Invalid topology, ownership, resolution, claim, and payout policy
- Independent pinned L1, latest L1, host, safe, and finalized clocks
- Factory, pending-game, and cached-game read-failure isolation
- Fresh proposer reconstruction over existing confirmed history

The scenario world now supports:

- L1 read faults keyed by boundary, target, and attempt
- Superroot query journaling with trust and L1 metadata
- Fresh proposer restarts over persistent world state
- Small history mutation controls required by the policy scenarios

The scenarios also exposed and fix a creation-safety issue:

- Game creation now requires a trusted superroot response before querying the UUID or submitting a bonded transaction.
- Trusted claim mismatches are terminal regardless of creator; untrusted observations remain retryable.
- The duplicate-creation guard is cleared when its tracked game becomes terminal or when factory history resets.

Treating a trusted contradiction as terminal may immediately release the creation guard and allow a
replacement at the same timestamp, putting a second bond at risk if the trusted response itself is
wrong. This is intentional: trusted supernode responses are the proposer's canonicality boundary;
retaining the guard would otherwise block recovery indefinitely at a frozen horizon.

Proof deadlines continue to use latest L1 chain time, matching the on-chain `block.timestamp` deadline check.

No launch, devstack, or acceptance-test configuration changes are required.

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: add permissionless deleteProvenWithdrawal to OptimismPortal2
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Adrian Sutton, Matt Solomon** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BTT5DGHA4/p1787791642391549?thread_ts=1787791642.391549&cid=C0BTT5DGHA4)_

**Before:** A withdrawal proven against a dispute game that later resolved `CHALLENGER_WINS`, or that was blacklisted, stays in `provenWithdrawals` forever. The record can never finalize, but nothing can clear it, so the portal accumulates dead state and monitoring gets no on-chain signal that a proof has been abandoned.

**After:** `deleteProvenWithdrawal(bytes32 _withdrawalHash, address _proofSubmitter)` lets anyone delete such a record and emits `WithdrawalProofDeleted`. No access control is needed: both conditions are permanent and independently verifiable on-chain, so the caller has no discretion and can only remove state that was already unusable. Retired and non-respected games are deliberately out of scope.

**How:** The function loads the proof, reverts `OptimismPortal_Unproven` if it was never submitted, requires the recorded game to be `CHALLENGER_WINS` or blacklisted in the `AnchorStateRegistry`, then deletes the entry. It leaves `finalizedWithdrawals` untouched so replay protection still holds, and leaves the append-only `proofSubmitters` entry in place — that stale entry now points at a zeroed record, which `checkWithdrawal` already rejects as unproven. Semver bumped to 5.9.0.

topPRs.title: kona-node: honor conductor timeouts and reject unsupported safe lag
topPRs.author: ogenev
topPRs.body:
## Description

Partially addresses #22667 by handling two sequencer flags that kona-node previously accepted but silently ignored:

- Applies `--conductor.rpc.timeout` to every conductor RPC request.
- Rejects nonzero `--sequencer.max-safe-lag` values before startup, since safe-lag enforcement is not implemented.

Updates operator documentation to explain both behaviors.

**BREAKING CHANGE:** Nonzero `--sequencer.max-safe-lag` or `KONA_NODE_SEQUENCER_MAX_SAFE_LAG` values now prevent kona-node startup instead of being silently ignored. Remove the setting or set it to `0` to continue operating without safe-lag enforcement.

## Tests

- Checks that all four conductor RPC methods apply the configured timeout.
- Uses paused-clock tests with durations below and above the default to verify requests expire at the configured deadline, neither early nor late.
- Verifies timeout configuration propagation and rejection of unsupported nonzero safe-lag values.

## Additional context

This PR does not implement safe-lag enforcement. That functionality can be added in a follow-up PR; rejecting unsupported values now prevents operators from relying on protection that is not active.

Related to #22667
